title: EIT Data Acquisition in Rat Sciatic Nerve Using Stimulation of Tibial and Peroneal Branches
author: Kirill Aristovich
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.ww7ffhn
materials: Prepare nessesary hardware: UCL EIT system (EIT system, Custom, n/a, Number of channels: up to 256Current frequency range: DC - 20kHzSampling frequency: 100kHzOnboard stimulator, https://github.com/EIT-team/ScouseTom , https://s3.amazonaws.com/pr-journal/bbq6a.png )
UCL EIT system https://github.com/EIT-team/ScouseTom/tree/master/src UCL EIT group
Sprague-Dawley adult male rats weighing 300 to 450g.
Load and process the data using the following software: UCL LoadData https://github.com/EIT-team/Load_data UCL EIT team
Forward solution PEITS https://github.com/EIT-team/PEITS UCL EIT team

steps.title: Prepare neural interface components
steps.instruction: Assemble the neural interface according to the published protocol (IOP Science article) while working inside a chemical hood because some components are toxic.

substeps.instruction: Follow the detailed preparation steps in the referenced paper (http://iopscience.iop.org/article/10.1088/1741-2552/aae868).
Perform all manipulations in a chemical‑hood cabinet due to toxic reagents.

steps.title: Induce anesthesia and intubate rat
steps.instruction: Anesthetize the animal with 5 % isoflurane in 100 % O₂ and secure the airway using a custom 3‑D‑printed small‑animal laryngoscope.

substeps.instruction: Deliver 5 % isoflurane in 100 % O₂ to induce anesthesia.
Intubate the rat using the small animal laryngoscope (Laryngoscope, Custom 3D printed; see https://www.thingiverse.com/thing:148315).

steps.title: Establish arterial and venous access
steps.instruction: Cannulate the right femoral artery and vein using BD Insyte/Vialon catheters.

substeps.instruction: Insert arterial and venous catheters (BD Insyte/Vialon, Becton, Dickinson U.K. Ltd.) into the right femoral vessels.

steps.title: Set up mechanical ventilation and gas mixture
steps.instruction: Connect an 18 G cannula and provide mechanical ventilation with a Harvard Apparatus Inspira ventilator using a 50/50 % O₂/air mixture.

substeps.instruction: Attach an 18 G cannula to the ventilation circuit.
Ventilate the animal with a Harvard Apparatus Inspira Ventilator (Harvard Apparatus, Ltd, UK) delivering a 50 % O₂ / 50 % air gas mixture.

steps.title: Monitor arterial pressure and maintain MAP
steps.instruction: Continuously monitor arterial blood pressure with a Cardiocap 5 and keep mean arterial pressure between 90 and 110 mmHg using labetalol and adrenaline as needed.

substeps.instruction: Measure arterial pressure using Cardiocap 5 (Datex Ohmeda).
Adjust MAP to 90–110 mmHg by administering labetalol and/or adrenaline.

steps.title: Initiate propofol infusion and monitor depth
steps.instruction: Start a constant intravenous infusion of propofol and assess anesthetic depth by the pinch‑reflex response.

substeps.instruction: Begin propofol infusion through the established IV line.
Check anesthesia depth regularly with a pinch reflex.

steps.title: Maintain body temperature on heated table
steps.instruction: Place the rat on a Thorlabs vibration‑isolated table and keep core temperature at 37 °C with a Harvard Apparatus homeothermic heating unit.

substeps.instruction: Position the animal on a vibration‑isolated table (Thorlabs Inc., USA).
Regulate core temperature at 37 °C using a homeothermic heating unit (Harvard Apparatus, Kent, UK).

steps.title: Expose sciatic trunk and branch nerves
steps.instruction: Access the sciatic trunk, common peroneal nerve, and tibial nerve following the published guide; make a 2 mm lateral incision in the biceps femoris near the knee to expose the common peroneal nerve.

substeps.instruction: Follow the surgical guide (https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1002/mus.21652) to expose the sciatic trunk, tibial, and common peroneal nerves.
Create a 2 mm lateral incision in the biceps femoris close to the knee joint to reach the common peroneal nerve.

steps.title: Implant stimulation electrodes on branches
steps.instruction: Place bipolar silver hook electrodes on the common peroneal and tibial branches.

substeps.instruction: Implant bipolar Ag hook stimulation electrodes onto the exposed common peroneal nerve.
Implant bipolar Ag hook stimulation electrodes onto the exposed tibial nerve.

steps.title: Configure stimulation waveform parameters
steps.instruction: Set the Keithley model 6221 balanced current source to deliver a square biphasic (positive first) constant‑current waveform: 1–3 mA amplitude, 50 µs pulse width, 5 Hz frequency (200 ms inter‑stimulus interval).

substeps.instruction: Select the Keithley UK model 6221 as the current source.
Program a square biphasic (positive first) waveform with 1–3 mA amplitude, 50 µs pulse width, 5 Hz frequency, yielding a 200 ms inter‑stimulus interval.

steps.title: Implant EIT array on sciatic nerve
steps.instruction: Place the EIT electrode array on the main sciatic nerve ~20 mm distal to the greater sciatic foramen and verify that two stimulating electrode pairs are positioned on the tibial and common peroneal nerves.

substeps.instruction: Position the EIT array on the main sciatic trunk in the posterior thigh, approximately 20 mm distal to the greater sciatic foramen.
Confirm that the tibial and common peroneal stimulating electrode pairs are correctly placed.

steps.title: Program EIT acquisition system
steps.instruction: Load the parameter file EIT_parameters.mat into the EIT system before data collection.

substeps.instruction: Open the EIT software and load EIT_parameters.mat.

steps.title: Collect EIT data for tibial stimulation
steps.instruction: Connect the stimulator to the tibial electrode pair and record EIT data while delivering 5 Hz stimulation.

substeps.instruction: Attach the stimulator output to the tibial stimulation electrodes.
Acquire EIT recordings during 5 Hz stimulation of the tibial branch.

steps.title: Collect EIT data for peroneal stimulation
steps.instruction: Connect the stimulator to the common peroneal electrode pair and record EIT data while delivering 5 Hz stimulation.

substeps.instruction: Attach the stimulator output to the common peroneal stimulation electrodes.
Acquire EIT recordings during 5 Hz stimulation of the common peroneal branch.

steps.title: Perform image reconstruction
steps.instruction: Run the inverse solution using the UCL EIT team reconstruction code (GitHub) to generate EIT images.

substeps.instruction: Execute the reconstruction script from https://github.com/EIT-team/Reconstruction.
Produce and save the reconstructed EIT images.
